subject: Add the authenticated loopback browser host to the MCP server process: designer assets, workspace snapshot, activity stream and catalogue actions
description:
MILESTONE e (browser), first task.

WHY: the spec's component-responsibilities section (the browser host row: an authenticated workspace API, never an exposed remote filesystem), its URL and browser behavior, and its local HTTP interface. Acceptance scenario "browser security".

GROUNDING:
- Contracts (task 9; decisions 14 and 16): icd/browser-host.json; BootstrapCapability, BrowserSessionRequest, BrowserSession, BrowserActionRequest {operation, arguments} and BrowserRejection; SanitizedLine and WorkspaceAccess; RefusalCause access-denied; ActivityEvent (task 6).
- SDK 1.31.0 offers createMcpExpressApp (dist/esm/server/express.d.ts:5-44; loopback default with DNS-rebinding protection), hostHeaderValidation and localhostHostValidation (middleware/hostHeaderValidation.d.ts:21,31). It has no Origin check.
- express 5.2.1 and express-rate-limit 8.7.0 are present only as transitive dependencies.
- The designer's production build is in apps/designer/dist/designer/browser.

CHANGE:
- Declare express, its types and the rate limiter in packages/mcp-server/package.json and the lockfile.
- Lifecycle:
  - The listener starts when a workspace opens with view, binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, and ends with the server.
  - It serves only the compiled asset root through express.static, with no dev server. No route reads or lists any other file. If no build is present, open says the view is unavailable and engineering operations still work.
- viewUrl: included in the first successful open; afterwards only when useful, without repeating setup text. It stays out of exports, signatures, notices and projections.
- Session:
  - A short-lived, one-use bootstrap capability in the URL fragment.
  - POST /api/session sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie.
  - Host and Origin are validated everywhere, bootstrap failures are rate-limited, Referrer-Policy is no-referrer, bootstrap material is never logged, and there is no wildcard CORS.
  - Failures checked before any operation runs answer with a BrowserRejection body.
- Routes:
  - GET /api/workspaces/{id}: the adapter-verified snapshot, trust states and capabilities.
  - GET …/activity: SSE with sequence numbers and a gap signal; summaries are bounded SanitizedLines.
  - POST …/actions: a BrowserActionRequest dispatched through the catalogue. The revision expectations travel in the arguments. A read handle's mutation, publication, check run or policy change is refused access-denied, and edit access grants no acceptance.
  - DELETE /api/session revokes only that browser session; agent handles stay open.
- Events: every one of the seven ActivityEvent kinds is emitted. qualification.progress, qualification.completed and cleanup.changed come from task 37's run table.
- Watchers cover only the opened paths, with debounce and bounded retention. After an external change they reload from the adapter and emit model.changed.
- Shutdown and close cancel and await owned jobs, then revoke sessions (task 14 hook).
- Auto-launch is off by default, at most once per workspace session, and its failure is non-fatal.
- Same-change docs: README §Components' Browser host row drops the clause "its ICD states the interface ahead of the implementation" (task 9), and README, icd/browser-host.json and Docs/workflow-integration.md describe the host as built.
- Tests in browser-host.test.ts:
  - security: invalid Origin; missing, expired and reused bootstrap; wrong handle; read-access mutation refused; edit access without acceptance; cross-origin; rate limit; cookie flags;
  - no file outside the compiled asset root is reachable (`..`, absolute, percent-encoded and backslash paths);
  - SSE order and gap; each of the seven event kinds emitted; external change reloads;
  - DELETE leaves agent handles open; two sessions get separate activity streams; a native check does not block browser events; a stale action is refused.

AREA TESTS: npm run build; node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/mcp-server/dist/test/browser-host.test.js; node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/mcp-server/dist/test/mcp.test.js.
WORKER: loom-worker (Sonnet 5, effort high, as its definition sets), resumed across its milestone while its context allows (task 1, warm reuse); Opus at xhigh only through `ledger escalate <task>` when the task proves complex, meaning an unresolved design question or a defect the worker cannot land (owner rule: prefer Sonnet; Opus xhigh only for complex work).
